verdictSummary: A single-user Notion is a weekend build: a block editor over a database, with a page tree and full-text search. What you cannot rebuild in a weekend is the part most teams actually pay for — real-time multiplayer editing with conflict resolution.
coreLoopDIY: A block-based editor storing pages as JSON, with nested pages and search.
whyPeopleStillPay: Teams pay for Notion because everyone is already in it. The document is not the product — the shared habit is. A personal clone solves the storage problem and none of the coordination problem.
notes: Best case for solo users who never share a page.
prompt: Build a self-hosted, single-user workspace app that copies Notion's core loop: a block-based rich text editor (headings, paragraphs, bulleted/numbered lists, checkboxes, toggles, code blocks, embeds) where every block is a row in a database, not a flat file. Add a page tree with unlimited nesting and drag-to-reorder, a simple 'database' view type (a table with typed columns — text, number, select, date, checkbox — that can also render as a board or list), and full-text search across all page titles and content. Support [[wiki-style]] links between pages with backlink tracking. Use Next.js and PostgreSQL, or your preferred stack, with the block tree persisted server-side so search and linking stay reliable. Write a one-off import script that reads Notion's Markdown/CSV export format and recreates the equivalent pages and databases. Do not build real-time multiplayer editing — that's out of scope for a single-user tool.

faq.q: Can I import my existing Notion pages?
faq.a: Yes — Notion exports Markdown and CSV, and the prompt includes an importer for that format.

faq.q: Will it work on my phone?
faq.a: As a web app, yes. As an offline-capable native app with sync, no — that is the main thing you give up.

faq.q: What does it cost to run?
faq.a: Hosting plus a database, typically under five dollars a month, plus API usage if you keep the AI features.

faq.q: Can two people edit at once?
faq.a: Not safely. Concurrent editing needs conflict resolution, which is well beyond a weekend build.
